In contrast, studies examining factors other than sex hormones have found no significant impact on outcomes after injury and hemorrhagic shock. For instance, one study found that alcohol and drug use were more important contributing factors to injury and poisoning deaths among young men.

It's worth noting, however, that the effects of hormonal differences on recovery from injury and hemorrhagic shock are complex and multifactorial. While sex hormones may play a role in certain aspects of health and disease, it is likely that other factors such as genetics, lifestyle, and environmental influences also contribute to individual outcomes.

Overall, based on the evidence presented, it appears that hormonal differences may not be the primary factor in explaining gender-based differences in outcomes following injury and hemorrhagic shock.
